The mean decay distance \( L \) in the laboratory frame is given by \( L = \beta\gamma c\tau \), where \( \tau = \hbar/\Gamma \) is the mean lifetime. Using \( \hbar c = 197.3 \text{ MeV·fm} = 1.973 \times 10^{-16} \text{ GeV·m} \), we have:

\[
L = \beta\gamma \frac{\hbar c}{\Gamma}
\]

First, compute \( \beta\gamma \):
\[
\gamma = \frac{E}{m} = \frac{8}{1.2} = \frac{20}{3} \approx 6.667
\]
\[
\beta\gamma = \sqrt{\gamma^2 - 1} = \sqrt{\left(\frac{20}{3}\right)^2 - 1} = \frac{\sqrt{391}}{3} \approx 6.591
\]

Then,
\[
\frac{\hbar c}{\Gamma} = \frac{1.973 \times 10^{-16} \text{ GeV·m}}{0.320 \text{ GeV}} \approx 6.166 \times 10^{-16} \text{ m}
\]
\[
L = 6.591 \times 6.166 \times 10^{-16} \text{ m} \approx 4.065 \times 10^{-15} \text{ m}
\]

This matches option (A).

Answer: A
